purpose: show that os4 fails A5 by a margin far smaller than the run-to-run variation of the quantities A5 is built from, and that no rule was changed to accommodate it
a5_definition: max(free+inactive) inside the settle window minus (free+inactive) at the anchor, over the process's kernel-resident drop; A5 passes when that ratio is >= 0.50 (verifier compares bytes: host_gain >= drop_bytes // 2)
rounding_note: the stored kernel_returned_over_drop is the ratio rounded to 3 decimals; both margins below are recomputed from raw bytes, so os4's stored 0.500 does not mean it reached the threshold
known_bias: the pool metric counts the process's own inactive pages, so it structurally saturates near 0.5x of the drop - the threshold sits inside its own artefact band, which is why os3's 0.508 passed while os4's 0.4996 did not
what_this_does_not_say: it does not say the pages were not returned on the new candidate: A6 (compressor is not the sink), A7 (process alive, evidence written after the window), A9 (app and kernel agree to ~0.06%) and the free-pool numbers all point the same way. It says the pre-registered rule did not clear its own threshold on this run, so the gate stays BLOCKED for this candidate.
recommended_next_step: pre-register a free-pool-only criterion (free gain over the drop, instead of free+inactive) and re-run; that metric does not count the process's own inactive pages as returned capacity - but adopting it now, after seeing os4 miss by ~0.04 points, would be moving the goalposts. It has to be decided and registered before the next run.
